facts.fact: Ila's crutch pace measures one and a quarter spans.
Ila took wall rubbings at Taravan at nineteen; she has never seen the Shilak Cairn carving clean, only about a dozen rubbings.
Ila has long hands from her mother.
The Under-Cairn's carved narrow hand is longer than Ila's by a nail's width; the broad hand is Saro's.
Pritam taught Kunal the old hill script as route-songs.
The Under-Cairn column holds fourteen marks, some with signs (knot, goat, wave); the shelf holds thirteen pairs of rotted gloves with a clean gap at the end where Harish's would be.
The party has half a skin of lamp oil left.
In the dark Ila deliberately keeps her gloves on over Kunal's bandaged hands, so no lie-cold could pass, and chooses not to listen to the stones.
